## Scope note (C13 split)

This row is the second half of the PLAN-11B C13 split of row 291:
P35.1b (PR #302) landed the fleet-hygiene sweep machinery — cruft-job
deletions, cron reconciles, AR cleanup, the sig-alerts disposition,
the partial live-diff. This row lands the consolidation — the
`[dispatcher]` declaration, the `sig-sched-due` hourly due
dispatcher, the name-checked `[[retire_triggers]]` list, the IAM
due-invoker semantics, the leg-runner, and (on the queued live leg)
the closing 0-drift live-diff proof + cost delta.

## Legs: run vs queued

### The engineering legs — RAN (offline, no ADC, no network)

- **`ops/cadence.toml`** — `[dispatcher]` (`job = "sig-sched-due"`,
  `scheduler = "sig-sched-due"`, `cron = "13 * * * *"`,
  `sa_class = "ingest"`, `task_timeout = "30m"`); `[[retire_triggers]]`
  — the name-checked set covering every `[[sources]]`/`[[batches]]`
  scheduler name **exactly once**: **89 `retired`** rows (every
  per-source/per-batch trigger except the kept pin), **1
  `kept-declared-pin`** (`sig-sched-camreg-batch-05`, the D-P31.4-1
  pin — stays live, keeps its own trigger), **3 `kept-manual`**
  entries naming `[[manual_jobs]]` members so the list is complete
  (job names, never triggers, never dispatcher-dispatched). Every
  retired row carries a required reason. `state = "paused"` lands on
  the **12 R6-gated rows** (the 10 `r11-*` batches + the 2 ADR-185
  tribal sources) — the pause rides the cadence row, not the retired
  trigger, so a wave resume is a data edit.
- **`ops/src/ops/scheduled.py`** — `DispatcherSpec` +
  `RetiredTrigger` dataclasses + `state` fields on
  `SourceCadence`/`BatchCadence` (`MaintenanceCadence` already
  declared `state = "paused"`); parse + `__all__`.
- **`ops/src/ops/dispatcher.py` (new)** — the due-set engine: the
  dispatch window is `(prev_dispatcher_fire, this_fire]` tiled by the
  dispatcher's own cron (`--since` walks every missed tick for
  catch-up); per-row last-fire evaluation over each row's cron;
  `paused`/`kept-declared-pin` rows are recorded as skipped inputs
  (never silently absent); enqueue is Cloud Run `jobs:run` through an
  injectable executor (`RestJobExecutor` mints an OIDC token for the
  dispatcher's own SA and calls the Cloud Run API — seam for tests);
  every evaluation/dispatch appends a `sig.dispatch-due/1` run row
  (GCS `ops/runs/` or local `.sig/ops/runs/`); an empty evaluation
  fails under SIG-ENG-042. Dry-run evaluates + records + never
  enqueues.
- **`ops/src/ops/live_diff.py`** — the consolidated declared shape:
  the dispatcher job+trigger join the declared fleet; a retired
  trigger found live reports the distinct *"declared retired — still
  live (pending)"* finding class, never ordinary drift;
  `retire_trigger_lint` (exhaustive name-checked coverage of every
  cadence scheduler, unique names, required reasons, no
  protected/manual collisions); paused rows' live triggers must not
  be enabled; no `[dispatcher]` → declared shape falls back to
  per-source (rollback map and live-diff stay symmetric).
- **`ops/src/ops/cli.py`** — `sig-ops dispatch-due`
  (`--at`/`--since`/`--dry-run`/`--declared`/`--cadence`/`--project`/
  `--region`, GCS or local run rows); stdout stays pure JSON —
  run-row location notices ride stderr; dispatcher surface in
  `cadence --check`; env-aware `--region`.
- **`ops/gcp/scheduled-ops.sh`** — `SIG_SHAPE=declared|per-source`.
  Consolidated (default): deploy `sig-sched-due` on the pinned fleet
  digest with **minimal env** (project/region/restricted-bucket/
  cadence-path+hash/declared-bundle URI — no Cloud SQL, no secrets;
  the dispatcher evaluates + enqueues, never ingests), bind
  `sig-scheduler` OIDC → dispatcher + the dispatcher class SA → the
  **77 due targets** (89 retired − 12 paused), create the one hourly
  trigger, report (never reconcile) retired rows. `per-source` is the
  recorded rollback map: every row's trigger reconciled, paused rows
  held PAUSED, an absent `existing = true` trigger (`sig-sched-muckrock`)
  recreated from its cadence row rather than erroring.
- **`ops/gcp/dispatcher-consolidation.sh` (new)** — the windowed
  leg-runner: `prestate` (full scheduler/job listings + per-trigger
  describes, sha256-sidecarred) → `deploy` (digest-pinned dispatcher
  job, `sig-scheduler` invoker on the dispatcher, dispatcher SA
  invoker on each due target, the one hourly trigger) → `verify`
  (digest/SA/args/schedule/target-URI/OIDC assertions + a staged
  `dispatch-due --dry-run` — evaluation end-to-end, nothing executed)
  → `retire` (fresh describe per name → `httpTarget` URI asserted
  against the cadence row's declared job → recorded delete; a URI
  mismatch or unexpected name aborts — never a glob) → `proof`
  (every retired name absent, kept pin + dispatcher present, closing
  live-diff, cost delta). `rollback` deletes the dispatcher
  trigger+job then replays `scheduled-ops.sh --apply --shape
  per-source`. Gates: closed-set parse/drift check **before any
  gate** (retired count pinned at **89** — a widened list refuses) →
  project → weekday 14:00–20:00Z window (else exit 42 queued) → ADC
  → `SIG_CONSOL_AUTHOR`. `SIG_CONSOL_NOW` overrides the clock for
  tests only; `SIG_CONSOL_STATE_DIR` holds evidence;
  `SIG_CONSOL_CADENCE_TOML` is the offline fixture seam.
- **`ops/gcp/config.sh`** — the `SIG_CONSOL_*` env block.
- **`ops/iam_identities.toml` + `ops/src/ops/iam_identities.py`** —
  `job_invoker` gains `targets = "scheduled" | "due"`: `sig-scheduler`
  binds the trigger-carrying jobs (probe + dispatcher + kept pin);
  the dispatcher's own class SA (`sig-ingest-rt`) binds the 77 due
  targets — a member on `due` that isn't `[dispatcher].sa_class`'s
  identity fails planning. Per-job IAM policies join the snapshot so
  the due leg diffs like every other binding. The dispatcher job
  lands in the declared map (`dispatcher = true` resolves to the
  ingest class) but its class **claim** is deferred to the
  consolidation leg's own amendment — the declared map carries 101
  jobs while the live `expected_job_count` pin stays **100** until
  the production leg lands (a claim would plan a binding on a job
  that doesn't exist; once it does, live-side "claimed by no class"
  enforces it).
- **Tests** — `tests/ops/test_dispatcher.py` (**40**: window tiling,
  open/close edges, paused + kept-pin skips, monthly/day-of-week
  boundaries, UTC-only DST sanity, malformed/missing `[dispatcher]`

## Deviations / notes

- **Authorization honesty** — the ticket text says B-13 approved the
  consolidation *design*; that is not a deploy authorization. The
  signed GATE-G4 enumeration predates the split and names 291, not
  291a. Treated as unlisted → queued + reported, never applied.
- **Declared 101 vs live 100** — `ops/iam_identities.toml` keeps
  `expected_job_count = 100` (the live pre-leg re-count pin) while
  the declaration map carries 101 (the pending dispatcher); the delta
  is documented and resolves when the production leg lands the
  dispatcher + the sweep's six deletions.
- **Pause rides the row** — `state = "paused"` on the cadence row,
  not the trigger: under consolidation there *is* no per-row trigger
  to pause; the due-set evaluator records paused rows as skipped
  inputs so a skipped row is never confused with an absent one.
- **Rollback symmetry** — `per-source` shape recreates every retired
  trigger (paused rows recreate PAUSED); a missing `existing = true`
  trigger recreates from its cadence row instead of erroring — a
  trigger deleted by consolidation must come back on rollback.
- **No ADR** — the consolidation executes the B-13 `a` answer and
  the ticket contract; it owns no new design decision.
- **Scheduler-of-record preserved** — cadence declarations remain
  authoritative data; consolidation changes trigger *shape* only.
